$comment: The last commit covered by a stage audit whose findings are written into docs/JOURNAL.md.
The stage audit used to be periodic — run at the end of a stage, against the tree. That was
right for the 43-finding audit, which caught things that had sat for weeks. It is the wrong
shape for what the evidence now says produces most defects: this project's own record shows
them arriving INSIDE the proofs and instruments written an hour earlier to close the previous
defect. The separator gap that gave the guard its only false negative, the crash the
history-reach fix introduced, the verdict state that printed in no output, and two wrong
entries in a licence notice were all fix-induced.
So the audit is scoped to a range rather than a moment. `npm run audit:scope` reports
watermark..HEAD, and CLAUDE.md's checklist is applied to that range instead of to the tree.
This file advances ONLY in the commit that writes the findings, and check:docs enforces that
by requiring this sha to appear in docs/JOURNAL.md — the same shape as a FEATURES.md row that
turns the check red when it is claimed without evidence.
ORIGIN, CORRECTED 2026-08-18. It first read 710cd94 with 'batches 1-7, each audited at close'.
That was ASSERTED from the presence of batch COMPLETION records, not established from audit
records, and it is wrong: docs/JOURNAL.md marks Batch 7 'PART DONE'. A batch that never closed
was never audited at close, and Batch 7 is 31 commits.
The origin is now a969ae4 — 'Record Batch 6' — the last commit of the last batch that closed.
Batches 1 to 6 each carry a journal entry with findings; 3 and 6 carry explicit stage-audit
sections. That is a defensible lower bound. 710cd94 was not.
The consequence is immediate and correct: the gate reports an audit owed for Batch 7 from the
day the mechanism exists, rather than starting green on a claim nobody checked.
This is the failure the origin was always going to have. It is the one value in this mechanism
nobody revisits, so an assumed origin makes every later range inherit the gap in silence —
which is precisely what the watermark exists to prevent. It survived one question.
audited: Batches 1-6; Batch 7 in four ranges (a969ae4..2aaa8f7, ..63242af, ..bcdf209, ..513b061), findings R1-1, R2-1, R3-1; 513b061..caa59d0 folded into the security-substrate amendment; caa59d0..d9f01b0 — identity, DocumentService and the advisory register — findings R-1 to R-8, both open ones since closed in f1737be and fe2274b; and d9f01b0..8f097e3 — the lane, the version counter and the command declaration — findings S-1 (the compile-fail harness accepts any error as a rejection, so a case can pass for a reason it does not claim) and S-2 (the engine seam's both-shapes claim has no control until a byte-image fixture exists); and 8f097e3..b315e2c — the compile-fail harness hardening, the guard's NUL widening and the engine seam — findings T-1 (a reachability verdict's path glob has a positive control and its SYMBOL has none, so a misspelt symbol leaves the verdict green forever; measured) and T-2 (the adapter's retention test asserts equal LENGTH where equal bytes were available and hold).
